title: Install Nessus on AlmaLinux 9
description: Install Tenable Nessus10.12.5 on a dedicated AlmaLinux9 VM, secure private HTTPS access and verify scanner readiness one small step at a time.
baseline: Nessus10.12.5 · Nessus-10.12.5-el9.x86_64.rpm · supported AlmaLinux9 x86_64 (current10.12 matrix9.6+) · VMware Workstation Pro
prerequisite: A host able to run the planned scanner and private target VMs, supported AlmaLinux9 x86_64 ISO, verified scanner RPM, approved lab network and valid Nessus entitlement. No dedicated live lab or user license is accessed by this website.

lessons.title: Meet Your Vulnerability Scanner
lessons.description: Explain what Nessus can check and write down permission to scan your practice machines.
lessons.what: Nessus is like a building inspector for computers. It looks for known weak spots; a finding is a clue that you must check.
lessons.why: A scan can help you fix weaknesses before someone misuses them, but it needs a clear boundary.
bestPractices: Scan only the two private practice VMs you own or have written permission to test. Record the owner, IPs, time window and stop contact.
Nessus is the scanner. Tenable Security Center collects and manages vulnerability information across scanners; installing Nessus does not install Security Center.
commonMistakes: An IP address being reachable does not mean you may scan it.
A Nessus finding is not proof that a computer was attacked.

troubleshooting.problem: I do not know which computers I may scan.
troubleshooting.fix: Stop and get a written target list. Use a private lab, not your employer’s network.

lessons.exercise: Explain the inspector analogy, then write a two-machine scan permission note without credentials.

quiz.question: What does a Nessus finding tell you?
options: A weakness may exist and needs review.
The host was definitely breached.
You may scan its whole network.
quiz.explanation: A finding contains evidence to assess; it does not prove a breach or grant permission.

quiz.question: What is Tenable Security Center?
options: A replacement name for AlmaLinux.
A separate platform that manages vulnerability information and scanners.
The RPM installer for Nessus.
quiz.explanation: Security Center and a Nessus scanner are different products.

steps.title: Name the job before using a tool
actions: Create a private notes file named Nessus-Lab-Plan.
Write: I will install one scanner, scan my approved AlmaLinux and Windows target VMs, fix one issue, and scan again.
Add a sentence: Scanning finds evidence; it does not automatically repair every problem.
steps.expected: The plan describes inspection, review, repair and verification in that order.

screenshot.title: Name the job before using a tool — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture only the non-secret plan text. Do not include employer names or credentials.

steps.title: Draw the permission boundary
actions: List the scanner and the two practice target VM names. Leave unknown IPs marked not assigned yet.
Record who owns each VM and the allowed test window.
Write a stop rule: stop the scan if a target becomes unstable or an unexpected address appears.
steps.expected: The allowed machines and stop condition are written down.

screenshot.title: Draw the permission boundary — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the scope table with private example machine names and no contact details.

steps.title: Separate the product names
actions: Open the official Get Started source below.
Write three labels: Nessus scanner, Nessus Agent, Tenable Security Center.
Mark this class as a standalone Nessus scanner installation. Do not use an agent installer or convert this scanner to Security Center management.
steps.expected: Your plan names the scanner product and leaves management conversion out of this exercise.

screenshot.title: Separate the product names — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture your product comparison notes, not a license or activation page.

lessons.pass: Your lab notes explain scanner versus Security Center and name only approved private targets.

lessons.title: Check the Scanner Requirements
lessons.description: Check AlmaLinux support, VM resources and the files before making changes.
lessons.what: We check the computer, the package and the license plan before we begin. Think of this as reading a recipe before turning on the oven.
lessons.why: The wrong CPU package or too little space can stop installation or plugin loading.
bestPractices: Use a supported, patched AlmaLinux 9 release. Tenable’s 10.12 matrix currently lists AlmaLinux 9.6 and later in the 9.x line.
Use a fresh dedicated VM. Do not install over an existing Nessus Agent, Manager or scanner; competing nessusd processes can be stopped by installation.
Keep all private license files and activation codes outside the repository and academy notes.
commonMistakes: The x86_64 RPM does not run on an ARM VM.
The 30 GB scanner disk requirement is in addition to the operating system and does not cap future log or result growth.

troubleshooting.problem: The host cannot spare the required resources.
troubleshooting.fix: Do not oversubscribe it. Reduce other running VMs or use a larger authorized lab host before proceeding.

lessons.exercise: Compare the plan to today’s official hardware and software tables and record your review date.

quiz.question: Which VM matches the supplied el9.x86_64 RPM?
options: An ARM AlmaLinux VM.
Any VM with a Linux logo.
A supported AlmaLinux 9 VM using x86_64.
quiz.explanation: EL9 identifies the compatible major family; x86_64 identifies the CPU architecture.

quiz.question: Can you commit your license file with the lessons?
options: No; keep it in private approved storage.
Yes, if the repository has screenshots.
Yes, if you rename it.
quiz.explanation: A renamed license is still sensitive.

steps.title: Check the supported operating system
actions: Open Tenable’s Software Requirements source.
Find the Tenable Nessus 10.12 table and the AlmaLinux row.
Record supported AlmaLinux 9 minor versions and choose an x86_64 installation image. Recheck the matrix if your image differs.
steps.expected: The chosen OS release and CPU architecture appear in your notes.

screenshot.title: Check the supported operating system — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the public support-table row with its page URL visible.

steps.title: Reserve enough VM resources
steps.where: Windows host · VMware Workstation Pro and notes
actions: Plan four virtual CPU cores and 8 GB RAM when your host can spare them. The standard scanner table lists four 2 GHz cores, 4 GB RAM minimum allocation, and 8 GB recommended.
Plan an 80 GB new virtual disk for this exercise. This is a teaching allocation: the scanner needs at least 30 GB beyond the OS, plus temporary space and future growth.
Check that the host has spare RAM, CPU and real free disk capacity. A growable virtual disk still consumes physical space as it fills.
steps.expected: The host can run the scanner plus the required targets without exhausting resources.

screenshot.title: Reserve enough VM resources — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the VM resource plan and host free-space view without unrelated personal files.

steps.title: Inventory the supplied files privately
actions: Keep Nessus-10.12.5-el9.x86_64.rpm in a private lab installers folder. Confirm it is the scanner RPM from Tenable, not NessusAgent.
Record the installer origin and trusted vendor checksum. Record only that a license is available, not its contents.
Treat nessus-updates-10.12.5.tar.gz as unidentified until its purpose and matching signature are confirmed. A filename alone does not prove it contains plugins.
steps.expected: The installer is identified; license secrets are separate; the update archive has not been blindly applied.

screenshot.title: Inventory the supplied files privately — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the RPM filename and non-secret origin/checksum record. Hide license files and private download URLs.

lessons.pass: The plan records supported AlmaLinux 9 x86_64, the resource allocation and a valid activation route.

lessons.title: Create the AlmaLinux Scanner VM
lessons.description: Build a fresh AlmaLinux 9 VM in VMware Workstation Pro.
lessons.what: We make a separate practice computer named NESSUS-ALMA09. It will run the scanner, not your daily desktop work.
lessons.why: A dedicated VM keeps scanner changes separate and gives us a clean place to diagnose problems.
bestPractices: Use the current supported AlmaLinux 9 x86_64 ISO from the official project.
Keep the practice VM on the approved private VMware NAT network. Do not bridge it onto an unapproved office network.
Use a new blank virtual disk. Do not select a physical or shared data disk.
commonMistakes: Easy Install may skip choices you need to understand; use manual installation here.
The scanner VM and Linux target VM should be different machines for the final two-target lab.

troubleshooting.fix: Check VM power, ISO attachment, Connect at power on and the virtual firmware boot menu. Do not repartition the host.

lessons.exercise: Power the VM off and on once, then explain which disk belongs to the VM and which disk belongs to Windows.

quiz.question: Which disk should the installer use?
options: The Windows host system disk.
A new blank virtual disk for this VM.
Any Western Digital disk attached to the host.
quiz.explanation: A separate virtual disk protects existing data.

quiz.question: Which machine runs these VMware wizard clicks?
options: The physical Windows host.
The Nessus browser page.
The future Linux scan target.
quiz.explanation: Workstation Pro runs on the physical host in this lab.

steps.title: Open the VMware creation wizard
steps.where: Physical Windows host · VMware Workstation Pro
actions: Click File → New Virtual Machine.
Choose Typical → Next.
Choose I will install the operating system later → Next. Select Linux and the closest supported Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 64-bit guest profile.
steps.expected: The wizard is preparing a new Linux VM and has not modified an existing guest.

screenshot.title: Open the VMware creation wizard — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the actual Workstation guest operating system selection page, with no unrelated VMs visible.

steps.title: Give the scanner its resources
steps.where: Physical Windows host · Workstation VM wizard
actions: Name the VM NESSUS-ALMA09 and save it in your private lab folder.
Create a new 80 GB virtual disk. Do not choose a physical disk.
Open Customize Hardware. Set 8 GB RAM and four total virtual CPU cores; do not exceed what the host can spare.
steps.expected: The VM summary shows the planned name, memory, CPU cores and new disk.

screenshot.title: Give the scanner its resources — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the VM hardware summary showing RAM, processors and disk capacity.

steps.title: Attach the installer and private network
steps.where: Physical Windows host · Workstation VM Settings
actions: Select CD/DVD → Use ISO image file → Browse to the official supported AlmaLinux 9 x86_64 ISO. Enable Connect at power on.
Select Network Adapter → Custom and select the private NAT VMnet recorded in the earlier lab-network lesson.
Finish the wizard and power on the VM.
steps.expected: The AlmaLinux installer boots and the VM uses the intended private network.

screenshot.title: Attach the installer and private network — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the VM network and ISO settings, then the AlmaLinux boot screen; use two genuine captures if needed.

steps.title: Install AlmaLinux on the new disk
actions: Choose Install AlmaLinux, then your language. Open Installation Destination and confirm only the new VM disk is selected.
Select Server with GUI if you want the same GNOME terminal path used in this course; a dedicated minimal server can also run Nessus.
Create a non-root lab user with administrator privileges and a strong private password. Complete installation and reboot.
Disconnect the installer ISO if it boots again. Sign in, open Activities → Terminal, and confirm the terminal is inside NESSUS-ALMA09.
steps.expected: AlmaLinux starts from the virtual disk and your administrator can open a terminal.

screenshot.title: Install AlmaLinux on the new disk — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the completed AlmaLinux desktop and hostname view. Never capture the password-entry screen.

lessons.pass: NESSUS-ALMA09 boots a supported AlmaLinux 9 installation and you can open a terminal as your lab administrator.

lessons.title: Set the Scanner Name and Network
lessons.description: Configure the approved private address, hostname, DNS and time.
lessons.what: We give the scanner a name and a reliable address. DNS is the address book; the clock helps secure connections agree about time.
lessons.why: Windows must reach the scanner, and online activation needs working DNS, time and approved internet access.
bestPractices: Record actual network values before changing anything. Example addresses work only if your private VMnet really uses that subnet.
Use the VM console for network changes so a lost SSH connection does not lock you out.
Keep DNS and time servers aligned with the lab design; do not replace AD DNS with public DNS on a domain-dependent target.
commonMistakes: The VMware NAT gateway is not necessarily the Windows host’s VMnet adapter address.
Typing a hostname does not automatically create a DNS record.

troubleshooting.fix: Use the VM console to reopen the same NetworkManager profile and restore the recorded settings; confirm the network adapter uses the expected VMnet.

lessons.exercise: Record scanner address, subnet prefix, gateway, DNS, Windows management address and active connection name without secrets.

quiz.question: What should replace the sample gateway?
options: A random public DNS server.
The actual NAT gateway recorded for your private VMnet.
The scanner’s own IP in every lab.
quiz.explanation: The gateway must belong to your actual virtual network.

quiz.question: What does hostnamectl set-hostname do?
options: Creates a public DNS record.
Changes the VM CPU model.
Sets the local Linux machine name.
quiz.explanation: DNS registration is separate from setting the local hostname.

steps.title: Discover the current network first
actions: Run the inspection commands.
Write down the active connection name, interface, IPv4 address and default route.
On Windows run ipconfig and record the IPv4 address of the adapter for this VMnet. This is the management source address used later.
steps.command:
hostnamectl
nmcli connection show --active
ip -br address
ip route

breakdown.meaning: Shows the local hostname and system identity.
Lists active NetworkManager profiles; use the displayed connection name later.
Shows a brief list of interfaces and their assigned addresses.
Shows network routes and the default gateway.

steps.expected: You have the actual guest and host adapter values; command output will vary by lab.

screenshot.title: Discover the current network first — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture ip -br address and ip route with only private lab addresses visible.

steps.title: Set a clear scanner hostname
actions: Set the scanner name using the command below.
Run hostnamectl again and compare its Static hostname value.
Record a matching private DNS entry or hosts-file plan if you intend to browse by name. Do not assume this command publishes DNS.
steps.command:
sudo hostnamectl set-hostname nessus-alma09
hostnamectl

breakdown.meaning: Runs this administrative change with your permitted elevated privileges.
Changes the system’s local static hostname.
The course example name; use your approved unique name if different.

steps.expected: The local hostname is nessus-alma09. Reopen the terminal if the prompt still shows its old name.

screenshot.title: Set a clear scanner hostname — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture hostnamectl after setting the name, with no credentials.

steps.title: Apply the approved private address
actions: Replace the four example network values and the connection name with the approved plan before running. The example assumes 192.168.77.0/24 with a gateway at .2.
Choose an unused scanner address; verify that .30 is reserved for this VM if using the example.
Apply the profile, then repeat ip -br address and ip route. Keep the VM console open while doing this.
steps.command:
sudo nmcli connection modify 'Wired connection 1' ipv4.method manual ipv4.addresses 192.168.77.30/24 ipv4.gateway 192.168.77.2 ipv4.dns 192.168.77.10
sudo nmcli connection up 'Wired connection 1'
ip -br address
ip route

breakdown.meaning: Edits a NetworkManager connection profile with administrator rights.
A quoted example profile name; replace it with the exact active name.
Uses the explicit static IPv4 settings.
Example unused scanner address with a 24-bit subnet prefix.
Sets the actual next-hop router for this network.
Sets the planned DNS resolver; these values are examples, not universal defaults.
Activates the modified profile and can briefly interrupt connectivity.

steps.expected: The interface has the approved static address and default route; DNS points to the planned resolver.

screenshot.title: Apply the approved private address — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the resulting private address and route. Do not capture unrelated interfaces or network secrets.

steps.title: Check DNS and the clock
actions: For an online scanner, test the documented plugin hostname with getent. If your policy uses a proxy, use the approved proxy plan.
Check timedatectl and confirm the date, time zone and synchronization match the lab.
An air-gapped scanner will not resolve or reach internet feed services; record that as an intentional offline route rather than changing security policy.
steps.command:
getent hosts plugins.nessus.org
timedatectl

breakdown.meaning: Asks the system’s configured name services to resolve a host.
The documented Tenable plugin service hostname, not a scan target.
Shows system time and synchronization status.

steps.expected: Online route: a DNS answer and a correct synchronized clock. Offline route: the offline activation plan is recorded.

screenshot.title: Check DNS and the clock — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the non-secret DNS and time results; do not capture a private proxy password.

lessons.pass: The scanner has its planned name/address, can resolve approved names, and the host can identify the correct private route.

lessons.title: Copy the RPM from Windows
lessons.description: Transfer the verified scanner installer to AlmaLinux using SCP.
lessons.what: We copy the installer into your Linux home folder. SCP is a delivery truck that travels through an encrypted SSH connection.
lessons.why: Copying the right file to the right machine avoids installing an agent or an installer for another operating system.
bestPractices: Use the approved SSH path and confirm the server fingerprint through the VM console before accepting a new SSH key.
Copy only the installer for this step. Keep private licenses separate and do not use them as public evidence.
commonMistakes: A Windows C:\ path belongs on Windows, not in the Linux shell.
The Linux account in the command must already exist and be permitted to log in.

troubleshooting.fix: Confirm sshd is running in the guest, TCP22 is allowed only from your management host, the VMnet is correct and you used the current scanner private IP.

lessons.exercise: Explain the local source path, remote account, remote host and remote destination in the SCP command.

quiz.question: Where do you type the scp command in this lesson?
options: The Nessus activation form.
Windows PowerShell on the physical host.
The AlmaLinux installer partition screen.
quiz.explanation: The file starts on Windows, so this command is run there.

quiz.question: What does a matching checksum establish?
options: The file matches a trusted reference value, if that value came from the vendor.
The license allows unlimited scanning.
The scanner is already installed.
quiz.explanation: A checksum needs a trusted comparison value; it does not activate software.

steps.title: Prepare the encrypted transfer path
actions: Check the SSH service using the commands below.
If openssh-server is missing, install it from the approved AlmaLinux repositories before starting sshd.
Keep SSH restricted to the Windows management source address using your existing private-lab firewall policy; do not expose it to the public internet.

In the VM console, display the SSH host public-key fingerprint. Compare this SHA-256 fingerprint with the first SCP connection prompt if that prompt uses ED25519. If it names a different algorithm, inspect that matching public host key instead; never accept an unexplained mismatch.
steps.command:
sudo dnf install openssh-server
sudo systemctl enable --now sshd
sudo systemctl status sshd --no-pager
sudo ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub

breakdown.meaning: Installs AlmaLinux’s SSH server package from configured repositories.
Starts SSH now and enables it after reboot.
Prints the status directly instead of opening a scrolling viewer.
Displays a key fingerprint; -l lists the fingerprint and -f chooses the key file.
The server’s ED25519 public host key. Compare the same algorithm; never display or copy the private file without .pub.

steps.expected: The SSH service is available for the approved management host.

screenshot.title: Prepare the encrypted transfer path — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the sshd status. Hide public addresses and any private key material.

steps.title: Copy the RPM from your Windows host
actions: Change the example path, Linux account and scanner IP to your recorded values.
Run scp. On a first connection, verify the fingerprint against the scanner’s console before accepting it.
Enter the Linux user’s password privately if prompted; no characters may appear while typing. Never paste a password into the academy.
steps.command: scp "C:\SONIC-Lab\Installers\Nessus-10.12.5-el9.x86_64.rpm" labadmin@192.168.77.30:~/

breakdown.meaning: Copies a file over SSH.
The quoted source file on Windows; replace this with its real path.
Example existing Linux user and scanner address.
Copies into that remote user’s home directory.

steps.expected: The transfer finishes without an error and returns to the Windows PowerShell prompt.

screenshot.title: Copy the RPM from your Windows host — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture only the transferred RPM filename and completed transfer; exclude passwords and host-identifying information.

steps.title: Compare the transferred file
actions: List the RPM and calculate its hash.
Compare the full hash with the trusted Tenable-provided value and the source file’s hash on Windows.
Stop if the name, size or hash is unexpected. Do not install a damaged or unidentified file.
steps.command:
ls -lh ~/Nessus-10.12.5-el9.x86_64.rpm
sha256sum ~/Nessus-10.12.5-el9.x86_64.rpm

breakdown.meaning: Lists the file with details and a readable size.
Your current Linux account’s home directory.
Calculates the file’s SHA-256 fingerprint; compare every character, not just its beginning.

steps.expected: The expected RPM exists and its complete hash agrees with the trusted source.

screenshot.title: Compare the transferred file — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the RPM listing and hash comparison without showing license files.

lessons.pass: The copied RPM is in the Linux user’s home directory and its SHA-256 hash matches the trusted installer value.

lessons.title: Install the Nessus RPM
lessons.description: Inspect the package and install it with AlmaLinux’s package manager.
lessons.what: We let dnf place Nessus files in their proper locations and record the installed package.
lessons.why: A package manager handles dependencies and makes the installed software easier to inspect later.
bestPractices: Use the matching verified EL9 x86_64 scanner RPM. Do not replace it with a similarly named Nessus Agent package.
Leave /opt/nessus as a real supported directory, not a symbolic link. Review any signature or dependency error rather than bypassing it.
commonMistakes: Do not use --nogpgcheck, --nodeps or random download mirrors to force installation.
Copying a file is not the same as installing it.

troubleshooting.problem: dnf reports a dependency or signature problem.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the full error, verify package origin and configured AlmaLinux repositories, and resolve the trusted package/key requirement. Stop rather than bypass verification.

lessons.exercise: Point to the package file, the installed package record and the installed administration command; explain why they are different.

quiz.question: Why does the install command include ./?
options: It means reboot.
It identifies a local file in the current directory.
It bypasses the firewall.
quiz.explanation: The local path tells dnf to use the file you copied.

quiz.question: What should you do with an unexpected signature error?
options: Force the install with verification disabled.
Delete all firewall rules.
Stop and verify the file, repository and trusted signing material.
quiz.explanation: Investigate authenticity and configuration before proceeding.

steps.title: Inspect before installing
actions: Change to the home directory containing the verified RPM.
Inspect its metadata and recheck the system architecture.
Confirm the package version is 10.12.5 and architecture is x86_64. Package metadata alone is not proof of authenticity; your earlier trusted hash check still matters.
steps.command:
cd ~
uname -m
rpm -qip ./Nessus-10.12.5-el9.x86_64.rpm

breakdown.meaning: Moves into your Linux home directory.
Shows the machine architecture.
Queries information about a package file; -q queries, -i displays information, and -p selects a file.
The local scanner RPM in the current directory.

steps.expected: The metadata and architecture match the planned scanner package.

screenshot.title: Inspect before installing — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the package name/version/architecture and uname result; crop out personal file listings.

steps.title: Install with dnf
actions: Run the install command and read the package transaction before confirming.
Approve only the expected Nessus package and legitimate dependencies from approved repositories.
Wait for dnf to return. Keep the actual success or error message in private evidence; this course does not manufacture it.
steps.command: sudo dnf install ./Nessus-10.12.5-el9.x86_64.rpm

breakdown.meaning: Requests authorized administrator privileges.
Installs software and resolves dependencies through configured repositories.
Uses this exact local EL9 x86_64 package, rather than searching for a different product.

steps.expected: dnf finishes without errors and records the package as installed.

screenshot.title: Install with dnf — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the actual transaction summary and final result, with no proxy credentials.

steps.title: Check the installed version
actions: Query the installed package database.
Check that the Nessus administration binary exists.
Do not start scans yet; service configuration, activation and plugins are still ahead.
steps.command:
rpm -q Nessus
ls -l /opt/nessus/sbin/nessuscli

breakdown.meaning: Asks the package database whether Nessus is installed and reports its version.
Shows details of the specified installed file.
The Linux Nessus administration utility; this is an installed executable, not the original RPM.

steps.expected: rpm reports the installed Nessus version and the CLI file is present under /opt/nessus/sbin.

screenshot.title: Check the installed version — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the actual package query and file path; do not invent a successful output example.

lessons.pass: The package database reports Nessus 10.12.5 for the expected architecture and the Nessus CLI file exists.

lessons.title: Start and Manage nessusd
lessons.description: Start Nessus, enable it after reboot and inspect its listener.
lessons.what: Nessus runs as a background service named nessusd. The web page depends on that service being alive.
lessons.why: A browser cannot connect to an application that is stopped, even when the firewall is correct.
bestPractices: Check for active scans before stopping or restarting a scanner outside this fresh lab.
Use systemctl for the service and Nessus controls for individual scans; they are different jobs.
commonMistakes: systemctl enable alone does not necessarily start a service immediately.
A running process does not prove that activation and plugin initialization are complete.

troubleshooting.fix: Read systemctl status and journalctl. Check free space and installation errors before repeating restarts.

lessons.exercise: Stop and start the fresh lab service once before any scans exist, then explain what each state check proves.

quiz.question: What does enable --now do?
options: Enables startup and starts the service now.
Starts one vulnerability scan.
Registers a license.
quiz.explanation: enable sets boot behavior; --now also starts it immediately.

quiz.question: What does listening on TCP8834 prove?
options: Every target is patched.
A process is accepting connections on that port.
Every plugin is initialized.
quiz.explanation: A listener is one check; browser activation and plugin readiness are separate.

steps.title: Start and enable the service
actions: Start the Nessus service and enable startup after reboot.
Check both enabled and active states.
If active returns failed or inactive, pause here and use the diagnostic lesson.
steps.command:
sudo systemctl enable --now nessusd
systemctl is-enabled nessusd
systemctl is-active nessusd

breakdown.meaning: Controls or queries systemd services.
Enables the service at boot and starts it immediately.
The Nessus Linux service name.
Checks boot configuration and current runtime state separately.

steps.expected: The checks show enabled and active for this fresh installation.

screenshot.title: Start and enable the service — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the actual systemctl results and service name.

steps.title: Read the service and port state
actions: Read the service summary.
Inspect the local TCP8834 listener.
If no listener exists, wait briefly for startup and inspect logs; do not open more firewall ports to hide a stopped service.
steps.command:
sudo systemctl status nessusd --no-pager
sudo ss -lntp 'sport = :8834'

breakdown.meaning: Prints the service summary without opening an interactive pager.
Shows listening (-l), numeric (-n), TCP (-t) sockets and their process (-p).
Filters to local source/listening port8834.

steps.expected: The service is running and ss shows a listener on the intended local address/port.

screenshot.title: Read the service and port state — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the actual service summary and TCP8834 listener without unrelated connections.

steps.title: Practice a controlled service restart
actions: Confirm this fresh scanner has no running scans.
Restart nessusd once, then check its state.
Note that a service restart interrupts browser access and can interrupt scans; do not use it as the first response to every problem.
steps.command:
sudo systemctl restart nessusd
systemctl is-active nessusd

breakdown.meaning: Stops then starts the service; it can interrupt work.
Checks whether the service is currently running.

steps.expected: The service returns to active and the expected listener reappears.

screenshot.title: Practice a controlled service restart — capture needed
screenshot.instructions: Capture the restart command and final state, not license information.

lessons.pass: nessusd is enabled, active and listening on the expected HTTPS port.

lessons.title: Allow Private HTTPS Access
lessons.description: Allow the approved management computer to reach Nessus on TCP8834.
lessons.what: The firewall is a door guard. We open one named door for the management computer, not for the whole internet.
lessons.why: The web console controls a security tool and must not be exposed broadly.
bestPractices: Use the actual active firewalld zone and the actual Windows management adapter IP.
Keep scanner outbound traffic and target-service permissions separate from inbound web-console access.
commonMistakes: Opening TCP8834 does not open SSH, target SMB or every scanning port.
The NAT gateway and management host source IP are different things.

troubleshooting.problem: The rule appears but Windows still times out.
troubleshooting.fix: Check that the rule is in the zone bound to the active interface, the source matches Windows’ actual VMnet adapter and Nessus is listening.

lessons.exercise: Explain why a source-limited rule is narrower than allowing 8834 from every address.

quiz.question: Which source address belongs in this management rule?
options: Any public address found online.
The actual approved Windows management source IP.
The scanner’s loopback address in all labs.
quiz.explanation: Match the connecting management computer’s real address.

options: Yes.
Only if the scanner is Linux.
No; scope and target access are separate.
quiz.explanation: A web-console rule does not grant authorization or configure all scan paths.

steps.title: Find the active firewalld zone
actions: Inspect firewalld state and active zones.
Identify the zone containing the interface used by the Windows management host.
Record that zone name. Use it instead of public in the next example if different.

sudo firewall-cmd --state
sudo firewall-cmd --get-active-zones

breakdown.meaning: The firewalld administration client.
Reports whether firewalld is running.
Lists zones currently associated with interfaces or sources.

steps.title: Add the source-limited web rule
actions: Before running, replace public with the actual active zone and 192.168.77.1/32 with the approved Windows host’s real management IP and /32.
Add the permanent rule, then reload so it becomes active.
Do not configure a router port-forward or broad public allow rule for this exercise.

Inspect the full active-zone rules too. An existing open 8834 port/service rule or a trusted/accept-all zone can defeat the narrow source rule. Have the lab owner approve correction of any overlapping allowance; adding a restrictive-looking rule does not remove earlier broad access.
steps.command:
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="192.168.77.1/32" port port="8834" protocol="tcp" accept'
sudo firewall-cmd --reload
sudo firewall-cmd --zone=public --list-rich-rules
sudo firewall-cmd --zone=public --list-all

Example active zone; replace it with your recorded zone.
Adds a rule containing source and port conditions.

lessons.title: Open the Nessus Web Console
lessons.description: Reach the scanner’s HTTPS setup page and identify its certificate.
lessons.what: We use a browser to talk to the Nessus service. The browser is a window; it is not the scanner itself.
lessons.why: You must confirm you reached your own scanner before entering an activation code or administrator password.
bestPractices: Use HTTPS and the correct private address. Confirm the certificate belongs to this controlled lab before making a temporary browser exception.
Plan an approved trusted certificate for ongoing administration instead of teaching users to ignore warnings everywhere.
commonMistakes: localhost on Windows means Windows, not the AlmaLinux VM.
HTTP and HTTPS are different schemes; use https:// with port8834.

troubleshooting.fix: Return to the previous port test; distinguish a timeout, connection refusal and certificate warning before changing settings.

options: https://localhost:8834 in every case.
https:// followed by the scanner private IP and :8834.

Disable browser certificate checks globally.
Send the password to the academy.

lessons.title: Activate and Initialize Plugins
lessons.description: Choose your entitled edition and finish scanner setup privately.
lessons.what: Activation tells Nessus which product you may use. Plugins are the inspection checklists it loads before scanning.
lessons.why: A running service with no usable plugin set is not a ready vulnerability scanner.
bestPractices: Use the edition and activation route allowed by your private entitlement. The installer does not grant every template or feature.
Use a unique scanner administrator password and store it in an approved password manager.
Treat offline registration URLs, activation codes and license text as secrets; do not paste them into this academy.
commonMistakes: Nessus Essentials does not support offline installation.
Do not declare initialization failed just because it takes longer than a few minutes. Check its actual status and system resources.

troubleshooting.fix: Check the chosen entitlement, correct time, DNS, approved outbound443/proxy access and available disk space. For offline use the next lesson rather than trying internet feed commands.

lessons.exercise: Write a non-secret readiness note with product edition, installed version and plugin date; never include the activation code.

quiz.question: What chooses which Nessus edition you may use?
options: Your valid entitlement and activation.
The number of screenshots in the class.
The VM name alone.

quiz.question: Can Essentials use the documented offline installation route?
options: Yes, with any tar.gz file.
No; the official offline-install page excludes Essentials.
Only if you install IIS.

lessons.title: Handle Offline License and Signed Updates
lessons.description: Recognize the supplied archive and use the correct offline activation and signed plugin route.
lessons.what: An offline scanner cannot fetch its own inspection checklists. An approved online computer must bring it the correct trusted files.
lessons.why: Nessus10.12.5 requires signatures for manual plugin updates. A random archive or mismatched license must not be applied.
bestPractices: Keep the license file, scanner challenge and custom feed URL private. Verify that the license is valid for this scanner and entitled edition.
Obtain the matching official plugin archive and signature together through the approved channel. Never rename an unrelated signature to make it look matched.
Follow a separate vendor procedure for application updates; a plugin archive is not automatically an application installer.
commonMistakes: nessus-updates-10.12.5.tar.gz alone is not enough to identify its purpose or satisfy10.12.5 plugin signature verification.
A private Tenable license file is not a plugin signature.

troubleshooting.problem: Only the archive is available, with no verified signature.
troubleshooting.fix: Stop the manual plugin import. Ask the authorized license administrator for the correct matched vendor archive/signature pair and verify the archive type.

lessons.exercise: Create a non-secret artifact checklist: installer, licensed edition, scanner-bound license available, plugin archive type verified, matching signature available, readiness date.

quiz.question: What is mandatory for manual Nessus10.12.5 plugin imports?
options: Only a file whose name ends in tar.gz.
A valid matching Tenable plugin signature as well as the archive.
An IIS website.
quiz.explanation: 10.12.5 added signature requirements for these manual plugin imports.

quiz.question: Can a filename prove the archive is a plugin update?
options: No; verify provenance, purpose and matching vendor artifacts.
Yes, if it contains the version number.
Yes, if it is copied over SCP.
quiz.explanation: Copying or renaming does not establish artifact type or trust.

steps.title: Identify the files before importing
steps.where: Windows host · private approved artifact inventory
actions: Check the provenance and vendor documentation/manifest for nessus-updates-10.12.5.tar.gz. Determine whether it is actually a Nessus plugin archive, application update or another package.
Check for its matching trusted signature file. The private license file does not replace that signature.
If the type or signature is unknown, write STOP — artifact verification needed and do not run an update command.
steps.expected: Every artifact has a verified role; unknown files remain unapplied.

actions: For a new offline installation, choose Register Offline in setup and obtain this scanner’s challenge code.

On the approved online computer, use Tenable’s official offline registration page privately with the challenge and valid activation entitlement. Transfer the resulting scanner license through the approved secure process.
For an existing scanner being put into offline mode, use the register-offline command only after confirming the supplied license is for this scanner and edition. Replace the example secure path.

sudo /opt/nessus/sbin/nessuscli fetch --challenge
# Existing scanner only; replace this path with its verified private license file:
sudo /opt/nessus/sbin/nessuscli fetch --register-offline /secure/path/nessus.license

Replace both example paths in the command. Alternatively use Settings → Software Update → Manual Software Update → Upload your own plugin archive and signature file.

lessons.title: Troubleshoot Without Disabling Protection
lessons.description: Check service, disk, networking, firewall and SELinux in a sensible order.
lessons.what: We test one layer at a time instead of guessing. A locked door and a sleeping service are different problems.
lessons.why: Evidence prevents fixes that hide the real problem or weaken the scanner.
bestPractices: Keep SELinux enforcing and firewall rules narrow. Review policy changes with the administrator instead of applying broad allow rules.
Keep diagnostic logs private; they may contain hostnames, network details and sensitive scan information.
commonMistakes: Repeatedly restarting a busy scanner can interrupt work without fixing DNS, disk or entitlement issues.
Do not disable SELinux or the firewall just to make a browser page work.

troubleshooting.fix: Check service and listener locally, then active firewall zone/source, VMnet route and host TCP test.
Check disk and memory, time, DNS, entitlement and approved update path. Preserve the actual error.
Inspect its exact AVC, reproduce in a test VM and review a narrow policy fix; never blindly allow everything.

lessons.exercise: Use one real or instructor-provided failure message and explain the next diagnostic check; do not intentionally damage a working scanner.

quiz.question: The service is stopped. What should you inspect first?
options: Add every firewall port.
Service status and relevant logs.
Delete the license.
quiz.explanation: A firewall change cannot start a stopped service.

quiz.question: SELinux reports a denial. What is the right approach?
options: Disable SELinux permanently.
Ignore all errors.
Review the exact denial and a narrow tested policy correction.
quiz.explanation: Keep protection enabled and fix the specific cause.

steps.title: Read service and storage evidence
actions: Run the status, journal and space checks.
Look for the first meaningful error, not just the last line.
Record the timestamp, error and available /opt space. Do not paste full diagnostics into a public issue.
steps.command:
sudo systemctl status nessusd --no-pager
sudo journalctl -u nessusd -b --no-pager -n 80
df -h /opt
free -h

breakdown.meaning: Selects log entries for the Nessus service.
Limits entries to the current boot.
Shows the most recent80 entries rather than the full log.
Shows readable free space for the filesystem containing Nessus data.
Shows readable memory usage and availability.

steps.expected: You know whether the service failed, whether startup logged a specific cause and whether storage is full.

On Windows rerun Test-NetConnection for the scanner’s current private address and port8834.

sudo firewall-cmd --get-active-zones

steps.title: Investigate SELinux carefully
actions: Check the SELinux mode and recent access denials.
If sealert is not installed, install the approved AlmaLinux setroubleshoot-server package before using its report command.

Read the exact denied operation with an administrator. Test a narrowly scoped approved correction in a matching test VM, restart only when needed, and check the denial again. Do not blindly generate a broad policy.

getenforce
sudo ausearch -m AVC,USER_AVC -ts recent
# If approved repositories are available and sealert is missing:
sudo dnf install setroubleshoot-server
sudo sealert -a /var/log/audit/audit.log

Searches the Linux audit log.
Selects SELinux access-denial message types.
Looks at recent events.
Analyzes the named audit log and offers diagnostic guidance; review recommendations, do not blindly apply them.
The system audit log path; keep it private.
Installs the approved AlmaLinux package that supplies sealert; an offline host needs an approved dependency/media plan instead of an internet repository.

steps.expected: SELinux remains enforcing; you either have no related denial or a specific documented issue for review.

lessons.title: Prove the Scanner Is Ready
lessons.description: Collect independent checks of the package, service, console and plugins.
lessons.what: We check the whole chain. One green light is helpful; several independent checks tell a stronger story.
lessons.why: This prevents a half-installed scanner from being marked ready for the administration course.
bestPractices: Record what you actually observed, including the date. Never copy example success text as evidence.
A ready scanner still needs target authorization, scan-policy review and credential planning before scanning.
commonMistakes: An active service alone is not proof of loaded plugins.
A screenshot of the welcome page alone is not proof that activation completed.

troubleshooting.fix: Leave the installation incomplete, return to the matching diagnosis and repeat only the failed check after a documented correction.

lessons.exercise: Give a two-minute handoff explaining each readiness check and the next step without revealing secrets.

quiz.question: Which set best proves installation readiness?
options: Only a ping reply.
Version, service/listener, private browser access, entitlement and loaded plugins.
Only the downloaded RPM filename.
quiz.explanation: Readiness spans package, service, connectivity and application initialization.

quiz.question: Should you mark the lab ready if plugins are still initializing?
options: No; wait or diagnose until plugin readiness is verified.
Yes, as soon as the VM starts.
Yes, if the firewall is disabled.
quiz.explanation: The scanner needs usable plugins before the next administration lab.

actions: Query the installed Nessus package.
Check enabled and active states.

systemctl is-enabled nessusd
systemctl is-active nessusd

Checks that the service is configured to start at boot.
Checks the service’s current running state.

lessons.title: Finish the AlmaLinux Installation Lab
lessons.description: Demonstrate a clean installation and prepare the next authorized scanning exercise.
lessons.what: Now you explain and demonstrate the work with your own evidence. You are showing that you understand the setup, not just that you can copy commands.
lessons.why: An administrator must be able to repeat, explain and safely maintain a service.
bestPractices: Keep scanner backups private because they can contain license/settings; follow Tenable’s backup procedure and storage controls.
Do not clone an activated scanner identity as a shortcut. Rebuilding or moving it needs the documented licensing/migration process.
Do not convert this scanner with fetch --security-center just to mention ACAS. That changes its management mode.
commonMistakes: Do not claim completion using the course’s capture placeholders. Those are requests for evidence, not proof.
Do not make a deliberately vulnerable production host for the final scan exercise. Use approved private target VMs.

troubleshooting.problem: You cannot explain a command you ran.
troubleshooting.fix: Return to its command breakdown, identify its machine/context and repeat only a safe inspection check before continuing.

lessons.exercise: Build or review NESSUS-ALMA09, demonstrate its restricted HTTPS console, explain activation and signed offline plugin requirements, and hand off a secret-free readiness record. Do not launch target scans until Class03.

Opening every inbound port on the scanner.
Converting the scanner to Security Center management.
